note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 52; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 2) on data/benches/standard.json: a standard solution and its dilution. c = (m / 249.69 g/mol) / 0.1000 L; diluted 25 to 100, a quarter of it.
title: Experiment: a standard solution

steps.title: The flask on the balance
steps.text: Click the first volumetric flask to pick it up, then click the balance. Then right-click the balance and click "tare".
steps.why: A volumetric flask holds its nominal volume at its mark, to within its class: 100 mL within 0.10 mL. Tared, the balance reads only what goes into it.

checks.text: the flask tared on the balance

steps.title: About 2.5 g of the crystals
steps.text: Pick up the jar, then right-click the flask for the menu. Type 2.5, then click "tip 2.5 g of the solid". Write down what the balance reads.
steps.why: Copper sulfate pentahydrate, CuSO4.5H2O, is 249.69 g a mole: 2.5 g of it is about 0.0100 mol. The balance's reading, not the 2.5, is what you took.

steps.title: Water to dissolve them
steps.text: Pick up the water bottle, right-click the flask, type 50 and click "pour". Then right-click the flask, click "stir", and click 60x on the clock.
steps.why: A solid dissolves in some of the water first; the flask is made up to its mark only once it has, or the volume would change as it dissolved.

steps.title: Until it is dissolved
steps.text: Watch the blue crystals go into the water.

steps.title: To the mark
steps.text: Pick up the water bottle, right-click the flask and click "to the mark".
steps.why: The bottom of the meniscus on the mark: the flask now holds its own 100 mL (within 0.10 mL) of a solution of all the copper sulfate you weighed. Its concentration is the moles you weighed over 0.1000 L.

steps.title: 25 mL of it in the pipette
steps.text: Pick up the pipette, then click the flask: it draws up to its mark.
steps.why: A 25 mL bulb pipette delivers 25 mL within 0.03 mL: a quarter of the flask.

steps.title: Into the second flask
steps.text: Pick up the pipette and click the second flask: it stands in its neck and runs out.

checks.text: the pipette on the second flask

steps.title: Until it is empty
steps.text: Wait until the pipette has run out, about half a minute.
steps.why: A bulb pipette is made to deliver its volume as it runs out freely, the last drop left in its tip.

steps.title: The pipette away, the second flask to its mark
steps.text: Pick up the pipette and click a free square. Then pick up the water bottle, right-click the second flask and click "to the mark".
steps.why: 25 mL made up to 100 mL: a quarter of the concentration. c2 = c1 x 25.00 / 100.0.

results.label: copper sulfate in the first flask (the truth)
